listening.title: Trump says US will form 'AI Force' and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar
listening.topic: US President Trump announces an 'AI Force' and an AI tsar appointment, dismissing safety concerns while emphasising America's drive to lead China in artificial intelligence development.
listening.topic_zh: 美國總統特朗普宣布成立「AI部隊」並任命人工智能沙皇，駁斥安全疑慮，同時強調美國要在人工智能領域超越中國的決心。
listening.transcript_excerpt: Welcome to 6 Minute English. Today we're discussing one of the most talked-about announcements in the tech world — US President Donald Trump's plan to establish a dedicated 'AI Force' and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar to oversee the nation's rapidly expanding AI sector. Trump took to social media to make the announcement, insisting that his administration would not hinder or stifle the growth of artificial intelligence in any way. He compared AI's potential economic impact to that of the Industrial Revolution, suggesting it could account for as much as twenty-five percent of America's GDP. Critics, however, are far less optimistic. A growing number of researchers — both current and former employees at major AI companies — have raised alarm bells, with at least one warning that there is a greater than ten percent chance of AI eventually killing all humans. These alarming claims have spurred calls for coordinated global action to slow development until proper safeguards are in place. Trump, for his part, has dismissed such concerns as a hoax. He also stressed that the United States must maintain its competitive edge over China, and that AI will almost certainly be on the agenda when he meets President Xi Jinping. So who is right — the optimists racing ahead, or the cautious voices urging restraint? Let's explore the key vocabulary and ideas surrounding this debate.

vocabulary.definition: to prevent something from developing, happening, or being expressed; to suppress or restrain
vocabulary.definition_zh: 壓制、阻礙（某事物的發展或表達）
vocabulary.example: The government was accused of attempting to stifle innovation by imposing excessive regulations on the technology sector.

vocabulary.definition: a measure or law designed to protect people or things from harm, risk, or damage
vocabulary.definition_zh: 保護措施；安全保障機制
vocabulary.example: Experts argue that robust safeguards must be established before autonomous AI systems are deployed in critical infrastructure.

vocabulary.definition: an informal term for a person appointed by a government to oversee and coordinate policy in a specific area
vocabulary.definition_zh: （非正式）政府任命負責某特定領域政策協調的官員，即「沙皇」
vocabulary.example: The newly appointed cybersecurity tsar pledged to strengthen the nation's defences against foreign cyber attacks.

vocabulary.definition: encouraged or prompted someone to take action; acted as a stimulus for something
vocabulary.definition_zh: 促使、激勵（某人採取行動）
vocabulary.example: The series of high-profile data breaches spurred lawmakers to introduce stricter data privacy legislation.

vocabulary.definition: to cause people to feel worried or concerned about a potential danger or problem
vocabulary.definition_zh: 引發警覺；讓人感到憂慮或警惕
vocabulary.example: The rapid spread of deepfake technology has raised alarm bells among both security officials and the general public.

questions.q: What economic claim did Trump make about artificial intelligence on social media?
options: A: AI could replace up to 50% of American workers within a decade
B: AI could contribute as much as 25% of the US GDP
C: AI investment would surpass defence spending within five years
D: AI could double the size of the US economy by 2030
questions.explanation: Trump explicitly stated on social media that AI could be 'as much as 25% of our Country's GDP', comparing its impact to the Industrial Revolution and the Internet.

questions.q: How did Trump respond to warnings about the potential dangers of AI?
options: A: He called for an independent scientific panel to investigate the claims
B: He acknowledged some risks but said they were manageable
C: He dismissed the concerns as a hoax
D: He agreed to slow AI development until safeguards were ready
questions.explanation: The episode clearly states that Trump 'repeated comments that criticism and concerns around the potential dangers of AI are a hoax', showing he rejected the warnings outright.

questions.q: What specific risk did at least one AI researcher warn about publicly?
options: A: AI causing a global economic recession within ten years
B: AI systems hacking into nuclear weapon controls
C: A greater than 10% chance of AI killing all humans
D: AI eliminating more than half of all white-collar jobs globally
questions.explanation: The content states that 'one suggesting there is a greater than 10% chance of it killing all humans', which was among the claims that raised alarm bells in recent weeks.

reading.title: Governing the Ungovernable: The Political and Ethical Challenges of Regulating Artificial Intelligence
reading.passage:
The announcement by US President Donald Trump of a proposed 'AI Force' and the appointment of a dedicated artificial intelligence tsar has reignited a fierce global debate about how best to govern one of the most transformative technologies in human history. Proponents of an accelerationist approach, including the Trump administration, argue that slowing AI development in the name of safety would cede critical ground to geopolitical rivals, most notably China. Trump has framed AI as the next Industrial Revolution, projecting that it could contribute as much as twenty-five percent of American GDP, a figure that underscores the enormous economic stakes involved.

Yet this optimism is not universally shared. A growing chorus of researchers, including senior figures at leading AI laboratories, has warned that the technology poses existential risks to humanity. Some estimates place the probability of a catastrophic AI-related event — one capable of causing mass casualties or even human extinction — at above ten percent. These alarming projections have spurred coordinated calls for a global moratorium on the most advanced AI systems until adequate regulatory frameworks and technical safeguards can be established.

The tension between innovation and precaution is not new, but the pace of AI advancement makes it particularly acute. Unlike previous technological disruptions, AI systems are capable of recursive self-improvement, meaning they can iteratively enhance their own capabilities without direct human intervention. This characteristic, often referred to as an intelligence explosion, is central to many of the existential risk arguments advanced by researchers in the field.

Governments worldwide are grappling with how to respond. The European Union has adopted a risk-tiered regulatory model through its landmark AI Act, while the United Kingdom has opted for a more flexible, sector-by-sector approach. The United States, under the Trump administration, appears to favour minimal federal oversight, relying instead on existing criminal and civil law to punish misuse. Whether this laissez-faire stance can adequately address the challenges posed by increasingly autonomous AI systems remains deeply contested among policymakers, technologists, and ethicists alike.

questions.statement: Trump's administration has proposed slowing AI development until comprehensive safety regulations are in place.
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states the opposite: Trump's administration favours an accelerationist approach and pushed back against calls to slow development, relying on existing law rather than new regulations.

questions.statement: Some AI researchers have estimated the probability of a catastrophic AI event at higher than ten percent.
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that 'some estimates place the probability of a catastrophic AI-related event... at above ten percent', directly confirming this statement.

questions.statement: The European Union's AI Act applies the same level of regulatory scrutiny to all categories of artificial intelligence applications.
questions.explanation: The passage describes the EU's approach as a 'risk-tiered regulatory model', meaning different levels of scrutiny are applied depending on the risk category, not a uniform standard across all applications.

questions.q: According to the passage, what distinguishes AI from previous technological disruptions?
options: A: Its potential to contribute a higher share of GDP than any previous technology
B: The speed at which governments have chosen to regulate it
C: Its capacity for recursive self-improvement without direct human intervention
D: The fact that it is primarily driven by geopolitical competition between the US and China
questions.explanation: The passage specifically identifies recursive self-improvement — the ability of AI to 'iteratively enhance their own capabilities without direct human intervention' — as the key characteristic that makes AI uniquely challenging compared to previous technological disruptions.

speaking.topic: Describe a time when you read or heard about a new technology that made you think carefully about its impact on society.
speaking.topic_zh: 描述一次你閱讀或聽到關於某項新技術的經歷，該技術讓你認真思考其對社會的影響。

part2.cue_card:
Describe a time when you read or heard about a new technology that made you think carefully about its impact on society.

You should say:
• What the technology was and where you first encountered information about it
• What specific aspects of the technology caused you to reflect deeply
• What positive and negative effects you think this technology might have on society

And explain why you think society needs to carefully consider how this technology is developed and used.
band_tips: Use a range of complex sentence structures and high-level vocabulary such as 'existential implications', 'socioeconomic disruption', and 'regulatory framework' to demonstrate lexical sophistication appropriate for Band 7-9.

Organise your response with a clear narrative arc — introduce the technology, describe your reaction, analyse both sides, and conclude with a forward-looking reflection — to show coherence and cohesion.

Demonstrate critical thinking by acknowledging multiple perspectives rather than simply stating one viewpoint; examiners reward candidates who can nuance their arguments with phrases like 'while proponents argue... critics contend that...'.

part3.q: Do you think governments have a responsibility to regulate new technologies like artificial intelligence, even if it slows down innovation?
part3.q_zh: 你認為政府是否有責任監管人工智能等新技術，即使這會減緩創新速度？
key_points: Governments have a duty to protect citizens from harm, and technologies with existential or widespread societal risks require proactive oversight rather than reactive legislation after damage has occurred.
Excessive or poorly designed regulation can indeed stifle innovation and drive development to less regulated jurisdictions, potentially making the global situation more dangerous rather than safer.
A balanced approach — such as risk-tiered regulation that applies stricter rules only to high-risk applications — can preserve innovation while protecting the public interest.

part3.q: How do you think the competition between countries like the US and China affects the way AI is being developed globally?
part3.q_zh: 你認為美中等國家之間的競爭如何影響全球人工智能的發展方式？
key_points: Geopolitical rivalry creates intense pressure to accelerate development at the expense of safety considerations, as neither side wants to cede a strategic or economic advantage to the other.

Competition can also be a positive driver of innovation, leading to rapid breakthroughs in medical AI, climate modelling, and other socially beneficial applications that might otherwise develop more slowly.

The risk is that a technology race dynamic, similar to the nuclear arms race of the 20th century, could lead to the deployment of systems that are not sufficiently tested or aligned with human values.

part3.q: Some people argue that the benefits of AI — such as economic growth and medical advances — outweigh the risks. To what extent do you agree with this view?
part3.q_zh: 有些人認為人工智能的好處，例如經濟增長和醫療進步，超過了其風險。你在多大程度上同意這種觀點？
key_points: AI undeniably offers transformative potential in areas such as drug discovery, climate science, and productivity growth, and dismissing these benefits in favour of a precautionary approach could cost lives and economic wellbeing.

The difficulty is that the magnitude of potential harms — up to and including existential risk according to some researchers — is so severe that even a small probability may justify significant caution, regardless of the benefits.
A more nuanced position is that the benefits and risks are not in fixed opposition; thoughtful governance can help maximise benefits while systematically reducing the most dangerous failure modes.

part3.q: What qualities or qualifications do you think a person appointed to oversee a country's AI policy should have?
part3.q_zh: 你認為一個被任命負責監管國家人工智能政策的人應具備哪些素質或資歷？
key_points: Technical expertise in computer science and machine learning is essential to understand the capabilities and limitations of current systems and to evaluate claims made by industry actors.

Equally important is a strong background in ethics, law, and public policy, as the most consequential decisions about AI involve value judgements and trade-offs that go far beyond purely technical questions.

Effective communication skills and political independence are also critical, as an AI tsar must be able to translate complex technical realities into actionable policy while resisting undue influence from commercial or partisan interests.

writing.task2_question: Some people believe that the development of artificial intelligence should be allowed to proceed as quickly as possible, as the economic and social benefits outweigh any potential risks. Others argue that governments must impose strict regulations on AI development to protect humanity from serious harm. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
writing.task2_question_zh: 有些人認為，人工智能的發展應盡可能快速推進，因為其經濟和社會效益超過了潛在風險。另一些人則認為，政府必須對人工智能的發展施加嚴格監管，以保護人類免受嚴重傷害。討論兩種觀點並給出你自己的意見。

useful_phrases.when_to_use: Use when arguing that a technology or phenomenon could fundamentally endanger human survival or civilisation
useful_phrases.when_to_use_zh: 用於論述某技術或現象可能從根本上威脅人類生存或文明時
useful_phrases.example: A growing number of researchers contend that unchecked AI development poses an existential threat to humanity that cannot be dismissed as mere speculation.

useful_phrases.when_to_use: Use when discussing the geopolitical or economic consequences of one country or group falling behind another in a strategic area
useful_phrases.when_to_use_zh: 用於討論一個國家或群體在戰略領域落後於另一方的地緣政治或經濟後果時
useful_phrases.example: Proponents of rapid AI development warn that overly cautious regulation would cause Western nations to cede competitive ground to rivals who face fewer restrictions.

useful_phrases.when_to_use: Use when recommending or describing a regulatory approach that calibrates oversight to the level of risk posed by different applications
useful_phrases.when_to_use_zh: 用於推薦或描述一種根據不同應用所帶來的風險程度來調整監管力度的監管方式時
useful_phrases.example: Rather than imposing blanket restrictions, policymakers should consider establishing a risk-proportionate regulatory framework that applies the most rigorous oversight to the highest-stakes AI systems.

useful_phrases.phrase: the imperative to balance innovation with accountability
useful_phrases.when_to_use: Use in introductions or conclusions when framing the central tension between progress and responsibility in technology policy
useful_phrases.when_to_use_zh: 用於引言或結論中，當闡述科技政策中進步與責任之間的核心張力時
useful_phrases.example: At the heart of the AI governance debate lies the imperative to balance innovation with accountability, ensuring that technological progress does not come at an unacceptable human cost.

useful_phrases.when_to_use: Use when discussing the specific technical characteristic of advanced AI that makes it uniquely difficult to control or predict
useful_phrases.when_to_use_zh: 用於討論先進人工智能特有的、使其難以控制或預測的技術特性時
useful_phrases.example: Unlike conventional software, the most advanced AI models exhibit recursive self-improvement capabilities, a property that fundamentally alters the risk calculus compared to earlier technological innovations.

outline.intro: Begin by acknowledging that artificial intelligence represents one of the most consequential technological developments in modern history, and that its governance has become a matter of urgent global debate. Paraphrase the question to present both sides fairly, then conclude the introduction with a clear thesis stating that while the economic case for rapid development is compelling, a measured regulatory approach is necessary to safeguard humanity from potentially irreversible harms.
outline.body1: Present the case for rapid, minimally regulated AI development. Argue that AI could generate enormous economic value — potentially transforming entire industries and contributing significantly to national GDP. Emphasise that in a competitive geopolitical environment, excessive regulation risks ceding technological leadership to rivals with fewer restrictions, potentially making the global situation less safe overall. Use the analogy of the Internet, which flourished under relatively light regulation, to support this position.
outline.body2: Present and then support the case for strict government regulation. Acknowledge that some of the world's leading AI researchers — people with deep technical expertise — have issued warnings about risks that range from widespread job displacement to existential catastrophe. Argue that the asymmetry of potential outcomes — where the downside involves irreversible harm to humanity — justifies a precautionary approach. Propose a risk-tiered regulatory framework as a middle ground that can protect against the most dangerous applications without unnecessarily restricting beneficial innovation.
outline.conclusion: Restate your position clearly: the question is not whether to regulate AI, but how to do so intelligently. Conclude by emphasising that governments, technologists, and civil society must collaborate to design regulatory systems that are adaptive, evidence-based, and internationally coordinated, ensuring that the transformative potential of AI is realised without compromising human safety or dignity.
